jsonld.name: Break-Even ROAS Calculator
jsonld.description: Finds break-even ROAS, break-even ACoS and target ROAS from price, VAT, product cost, shipping and fees for one or many products.

jsonld.name: Break-Even ROAS Calculator: Break-Even ROAS and ACoS

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the return on ad spend at which an ad earns back exactly what it cost. Break-even ROAS = selling price ÷ profit per sale before ads, which is the same as 1 ÷ the profit margin before ads. A product with a $60 price and $28.20 profit before ads breaks even at a ROAS of 2.13.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate break-even ROAS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Work out the profit per sale before ads: net revenue after VAT, minus product cost, shipping, payment fees and other costs. Then divide the selling price by that profit. If a $60 sale leaves $28.20 before ads, break-even ROAS is 60 ÷ 28.20 = 2.13.

mainEntity.name: What is break-even ACoS and how does it relate to ROAS?

acceptedAnswer.text: ACoS (advertising cost of sales) is ad spend divided by sales, so it is 1 ÷ ROAS. Break-even ACoS is the highest ACoS you can run without losing money. A break-even ROAS of 2.13 is a break-even ACoS of 47.0%.

mainEntity.name: Should the selling price include VAT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, enter the price the customer pays, because ad platforms report revenue with VAT or sales tax included. The calculator removes the tax before working out your profit, so your ROAS target is not overstated. Set the VAT rate to 0 if you do not charge tax.

There is no single good number, because it depends on your margin. A 20% margin before ads needs ROAS 5.00 just to break even, while a 50% margin needs only 2.00. A good ROAS is one comfortably above your own break-even ROAS.

mainEntity.name: How is target ROAS different from break-even ROAS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Break-even ROAS only covers costs. Target ROAS also leaves the profit you want: it takes the profit before ads, subtracts your target margin on net revenue, and divides the price by what is left for ad spend. A 10% target margin raises the example product from ROAS 2.13 to 2.59.

mainEntity.name: How do I work out ROAS for several products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add each product with its own price, costs and units sold. The calculator blends them by units, so the combined ROAS is total revenue ÷ total profit before ads. Use it for a campaign that promotes a mix of products, then check each product's own ROAS in the table.

mainEntity.name: Do returns and refunds change break-even ROAS?

acceptedAnswer.text: They do. Returns lower the revenue you keep, so the real profit per sale is smaller than the listed price suggests. Add the average return cost per sale to the Other cost per unit field to include it.

mainEntity.name: Does a ROAS above break-even always mean the ads are worth running?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. It means each sale covers its own costs and ad spend, but it ignores fixed costs such as salaries, software and rent. Use the Break-Even Calculator to see how many sales you need to cover those as well.
